Two H-bond motifs exist: (a) the tertiary OH (O15–H16) donating to the ketone O3 through a 6-membered ring (H–O15–C7–C4–C2=O3); (b) the secondary ring OH (O10–H11), which is cis to the side chain, donating to O3 through a 7-membered ring. Measured H···O distances / O–H···O angles: 9 (1.87/157), 4 (1.88/157), 18 (1.91/157), 8 (1.95/150), 20 (1.96/149), 3 (2.03/141) - all motif (b), short and nearly linear, i.e. strong bonds; 26 (1.97/138), 19 (2.05/132), 22 (2.06/130), 23 (2.07/131), 29 (2.14/127) - motif (a), the constrained 6-ring, giving good O···O (2.79-2.83) but bent, hence moderate; 27 (2.32/125), 12 (2.34/126), 28 (2.46/112), 13 (2.48/117 and 2.62/121, bifurcated-poor), 30 (2.50/127) - only weak, badly aligned contacts; 5 and 10 (2.80) and 1 (3.05) essentially none. Conformers 7, 11, 24, 16, 2, 6, 17, 21, 15, 25, 14 have no OH within 3.4 Ang of any acceptor at all (all O···O > 3.5, hydroxyl H's pointing into space) and thus lose 3-4 kcal of H-bond stabilization.

To rank within groups (and to place the non-bonded set) I summed unit group-dipoles (carbonyl C2->O3; each hydroxyl as unit(O-C)+unit(O-H)), taking a small total dipole as a proxy for favourable, mutually cancelling electrostatics. Values: 27 (0.9), 11 (1.3), 24 (1.7), 28 (1.8), 6 (1.8), 7 (1.9), 17 (2.0), 13 (2.0), 29 (2.1), 12 (2.2), 3 (2.2), 9 (2.4), 20 (2.4), 18 (2.6), 19 (2.7), 30 (2.8), 10 (2.9), 26 (3.1), 1 (3.0), 14 (3.1), 21 (3.2), 2 (3.3), 16 (3.5), 22 (3.6), 5 (3.6), 8 (4.0), 4 (4.4), 6-ring 26 etc. Thus the best structures combine the short, linear 7-ring H-bond with modest residual dipole (9, 18, 20, 3), while 4 and 8 keep an excellent H-bond but have the remaining C-O and C=O dipoles reinforcing (large residual dipole), so they are placed just behind. The 6-ring donors (23, 26, 19, 29, 22) come next; the weak/bent contacts (27, 12, 13, 28, 30) follow; and the completely non-H-bonded, extended conformers are last, ordered by how well their three polar groups cancel (10, 11, 24, 6, 7, 17 better; 14, 21, 2, 16 worst, with all dipoles roughly aligned). No conformer shows a serious steric clash: methyl and CH2 hydrogens stay > 2.1 Ang from ring hydrogens, so sterics are only a minor tiebreaker.

Uncertainty: the gap between the strong 7-ring donors (9, 18, 20, 3, 4, 8) is small (a few tenths kcal) and depends on how much weight the residual dipole term deserves - 4 and 8 could well be top-three in a real DFT ranking. Likewise the borderline cases 27 (weak H-bond but best dipole cancellation) versus 30/28, and the entire non-H-bonded block, are ordered by a crude electrostatic argument and could easily reshuffle by ~1 kcal.

All 30 structures are the same molecule: CH3-CH(OH)-CH(CHO)(COCH3), i.e. 2-(1-hydroxyethyl)-3-oxobutanal (C6H10O3). Connectivity check on any block: C1H3-C3H(O4H5)-C7H(-C8H=O9 aldehyde)(-C11(=O12)-C13H3 ketone). There is no ring, so ring strain is irrelevant; the discriminating factors are (i) the intramolecular O4-H5...O=C hydrogen bond (only a 5-heavy-atom S(5)-type contact is geometrically possible, so H-bonds are bent, O-H...O ~120-140 deg), (ii) dipole-dipole repulsion between the two carbonyls attached to the same carbon C7 (a 1,3-dicarbonyl motif that strongly prefers the two C=O vectors anti/skew rather than parallel), and (iii) ordinary gauche/eclipsing strain.

I measured d(H5...O9) and d(H5...O12) plus the O-H...O angle, and the angle between the two C=O bond vectors (v1 = O9-C8, v2 = O12-C11; ~180 deg = anti dipoles = favorable, ~60-70 deg = parallel dipoles = repulsive).

13 (152 deg; H5...O12 = 3.02 A but O-H...O only ~107 deg, so no real H-bond), 30 (146), 25 (144), 11 (142), 8 (141), 27 (138), 3 (127), 16 (122), 7 (114), 1 (113), 9 (109), 28 (108), 6 (108), 26 (102), 2 (95) are progressively worse; 20 (71), 12 (65) and 19 (60) have the two C=O groups nearly parallel (strong dipole repulsion, with O...O ~3.3 A in 12) and additionally lack any OH stabilization, so they are the least stable.

No structure shows a hard steric clash (all nonbonded H...H > ~2.0 A, no O...O below 2.7 A except the H-bonded pairs, where O...O ~2.7-2.8 A as expected).

Uncertainty: the top three (17, 15, 10) are within a fraction of a kcal/mol of each other - 17 has the shortest H-bond to the better (ketone) acceptor while 15 has the ideal anti-carbonyl arrangement with a slightly longer H-bond to the aldehyde, so their order could swap. Likewise 4 versus 23/5, and the tightly bunched non-bonded block (13, 30, 25, 11, 8, 27) differ by only tenths of a kcal/mol and their relative order is essentially within the noise of this geometric analysis.

All 30 structures are the same molecule, 2-ethyl-5-(hydroxymethyl)-1H-pyrrole (aromatic pyrrole ring, N-H, exocyclic CH2OH on one alpha carbon, ethyl on the other). Ring geometry (bond lengths 1.36-1.41 A, planar 5-ring) is essentially identical in every structure, so there is no ring-strain difference; the whole conformational energy comes from (i) rotation of the ethyl group about C(ring)-CH2, (ii) rotation of the CH2-O bond relative to the ring plane, (iii) the C-C-O-H rotamer, and (iv) any weak intramolecular contacts.

H-bond survey: the pyrrole N is not an acceptor (lone pair in the aromatic pi system), so the only candidate interactions are N-H...O (a 5-membered pseudo-ring) or O-H...pi. I computed H(N)...O for all conformers: it ranges 2.41-4.11 A. Only conformers 12 and 20 have a short value (2.41 A, N...O 2.70 A) which corresponds to the N-C(ring)-CH2-O torsion near syn (~22 deg). However the N-H...O angle in these is only ~96 deg, i.e. the N-H vector points away from the oxygen, so this is not a directional hydrogen bond, just a near-eclipsed O/N 1,4 contact whose electrostatic attraction (H+...O-) is largely cancelled by the N...O repulsion. For O-H...pi I checked the height of the hydroxyl H above the ring plane and whether d(H_O...C_ipso) < d(O...C_ipso) (2.42 A, fixed by the chain): in every conformer d(H_O...C9) = 2.49-2.58 A (or 3.2 A when the O-H is anti), i.e. the O-H bond is roughly perpendicular to the O...ring vector and points outward. So NO conformer has a genuine OH...pi or N-H...O bond; the ensemble is intrinsically flat and the ranking below is based on torsional/steric preferences only, with expected spreads well under 1 kcal/mol.

Quantitative descriptors used (ring plane from N, C3, C4; n = unit normal):
- d(CH3) = out-of-plane displacement of the ethyl methyl carbon. 1.4 A = methyl perpendicular to the ring (the preferred arrangement for a 2-alkyl heteroarene, avoiding eclipsing/1,5 H...H contact with the neighbouring ring C-H or N-H); ~0 A = methyl in the ring plane (in-plane methyl H...H(ring C3) ~2.6 A, mild repulsion / near the torsional maximum).
- d(O) = out-of-plane displacement of the hydroxyl oxygen. 1.1-1.35 A = C-O roughly perpendicular to the ring (benzyl-alcohol-like minimum, stabilized by pi(ring)->sigma*(C-O) hyperconjugation); 0.2-0.5 A = C-O in the ring plane (either anti, N...O ~3.68 A, or syn, N...O ~2.70 A, the latter partly eclipsed).

Results: perpendicular ethyl AND perpendicular C-O (best combination): 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11, 13, 16, 18, 19, 21, 27 (d(CH3)=1.41-1.47, d(O)=1.09-1.34). Perpendicular ethyl but C-O in plane (anti): 4 (d_O 0.21), 15 (0.31), 14 (0.40), 10 (0.43). Perpendicular ethyl with near-syn (partly eclipsed) C-O and the short but badly angled N-H...O contact: 12, 20. Twisted ethyl (~25-35 deg from the plane, i.e. sitting on the flank of the in-plane form): 23, 28 (C-O perpendicular) and 9, 30 (C-O in plane). Fully in-plane methyl pointing at the C3-H side: 2, 17, 29, 26, 24 (C-O perpendicular) and 1, 22 (C-O also in plane, i.e. two unfavourable torsions at once). Worst case 25: the methyl lies in the ring plane on the N-H side, giving H(methyl)...H(N) contacts of only 2.35-2.41 A, a genuine steric repulsion not present anywhere else.

Within the top family the conformers differ only in the sign of the torsions and in the OH rotamer (almost all gauche, H_O 2.5 A from the ipso carbon; 12/20 are anti); these are near-degenerate, so I order them by how cleanly both key torsions sit at their ideal perpendicular values (sum of d(CH3)+d(O)): 19, 3, 6, 13, 7, 21 slightly ahead of 18, 16, 8, then 5, 27, 11 whose C-O is only ~45-60 deg out of plane. 12 and 20 are essentially a mirror-image pair and are kept adjacent, as are 9/30 and 1/22. Main uncertainties: (a) whether the in-plane C-O (conformers 4, 15, 14, 10) is really ~0.3 kcal/mol above the perpendicular one - if the pi/lone-pair repulsion argument dominates over hyperconjugation these four would move up into the top group; (b) the exact placement of the near-syn pair 12/20, which would rise if the 2.41 A H(N)...O contact is treated as a stabilizing electrostatic interaction rather than an eclipsing penalty; (c) the ordering inside the leading twelve is within noise.

All 30 files are the same molecule: HC≡C–CH2–C(CH3)(OH)–CH2–CHO (3-hydroxy-3-methylhex-5-ynal). Connectivity check per file: C1 = methyl (H2,H3,H4), C5 = quaternary carbinol carbon bearing O6–H7, C8H2 (H12,H13) linking to the aldehyde C9(=O10)H11, and C14H2 (H18,H19) linking to the alkyne C15≡C16–H17. Since there is no ring and no rotatable-bond strain beyond torsions, relative stability is dominated by (i) the intramolecular O–H···O=C hydrogen bond, which closes a favourable 6-membered ring (O6–H7···O10=C9–C8–C5), (ii) much weaker O–H···π(alkyne) or C–H···O contacts, and (iii) ordinary gauche/eclipsing and O···O lone-pair repulsions.

Step 1 – search for the β-hydroxy-aldehyde H-bond (H7···O10 distance and O–H···O angle):
Conf 1: 1.94 Å, 142° (O···O 2.76) – best geometry, near-ideal 6-ring.
Conf 16: 2.07 Å, 133° (O···O 2.82).
Conf 2: 2.08 Å, 132° (O···O 2.82).
Conf 6: 2.11 Å, 130° (O···O 2.83).
Conf 21: 2.12 Å, 129° (O···O 2.83).
Conf 26: 2.14 Å, 128° (O···O 2.85).
No other conformer has H7 within 3.3 Å of O10 with a useful angle, so these six form a clearly lower-energy tier (a 6-membered OH···O=C bond is worth several kcal/mol). Within the tier the ranking follows shortening H···O and opening of the O–H···O angle; the differences after conf 1 are small (0.05–0.07 Å, 2–5°) and therefore uncertain.

Step 2 – a second, recurring family (13 structures) places the hydroxyl gauche to the propargyl branch, with H7 only 2.36–2.52 Å from the propargylic sp carbon C15 (midpoint distances 2.5–2.7 Å). Because the ring formed (H–O–C5–C14–C15) is only five-membered, the O–H···C angle is forced to 105–123°, so this is at best a weak, badly aligned O–H···π(alkyne) contact rather than a real H-bond: 22 (2.36 Å, 123°), 28 (2.38, 123°), 19 (2.43, 122°), 9 (2.47), 7 (2.43), 23 (2.44, 118°), 30 (2.46, 118°), 12 (2.47, 118°), 4 (2.47, 118°), 11 (2.48), 8 (2.51, 118°), 17 (2.52), 13 (2.47 but additionally O6···O10 = 3.53 Å with the OH pointing away, i.e. lone-pair/dipole repulsion). Small bonuses were given where an extra C–H···O=C contact exists (19: H19···O10 = 2.36 Å; 9: methyl H2···O10 = 2.43 Å); a penalty was given to 13 for the unrelieved O···O approach.

Step 3 – the remaining 11 conformers (5, 10, 14, 15, 18, 20, 24, 25, 27, 29, 3) have a completely free hydroxyl (H7 > 3.0 Å from both the carbonyl O and the alkyne) and extended, essentially staggered backbones; they lose the H-bond stabilisation entirely and also keep both C=O and O–H dipoles unpaired. Fine distinctions: 25 has a stabilising CH2···O=C contact (H19···O10 2.37 Å) and 24/25 still keep the O gauche to the alkyne (H7···C15 ≈ 3.1 Å), so they sit at the top of this group; 20, 18, 29, 5, 27 are cleanly staggered with no clashes; 15, 14, 10 are similar but with more crowded methyl/CH2 arrangements; conf 3 is placed last because the two oxygens approach to 3.34–3.42 Å with the O–H rotated ~87° away, giving lone-pair/lone-pair and dipole–dipole repulsion without any compensating hydrogen bond.

Uncertainty: only the tier separation (H-bonded ≫ weak OH···π ≳ free OH) is robust. Ordering within tier 1 rests on differences of a few hundredths of an Å in the H-bond, and the ordering inside tiers 2 and 3 involves sub-kcal/mol torsional and weak-contact effects that could easily reshuffle.

Structure identification: all 30 files contain the same skeleton, C7H14O2 with one ring (1 degree of unsaturation): a tetrahydrofuran ring O9-C10-C2-C3-C6, with a methyl (C1) on the ring carbon C2 and a 2-hydroxyethyl chain (C11-C13-O15H16) on the adjacent ring carbon C10 (i.e. cis-2-(2-hydroxyethyl)-3-methyl-THF; the C1-C2-C10-C11 torsion is small, 0-45 deg, in every conformer, so all share the same cis stereochemistry).

Dominant energetic factor: an intramolecular O15-H16...O9(ring ether) hydrogen bond, which closes a favourable six-membered (H,O,C,C,C,O) ring. Measured H16...O9 distances/O-H...O angles: conf 14 (1.98 A, 140 deg), 29 (1.98, 139), 28 (1.98, 139), 11 (2.00, 140), 8 (2.01, 135), 23 (2.09, 128). All other conformers have H16...O9 > 3.2 A (no H-bond) except conf 13, which has a long, badly bent contact (2.58 A, 119 deg) worth only a fraction of a real H-bond. Ether O...O separations in the non-bonded conformers are all 3.6-4.8 A, so no lone-pair/lone-pair repulsion penalty distinguishes them.

Second factor: chain torsions. Using O9...C13 and O15...C10 distances as torsion proxies: (i) tau1 = O9-C10-C11-C13 can put C13 anti to the ring CH (C2) - cheapest, since it points the chain away from the cis-methyl - or anti to the ring O (then C13 is gauche to the substituted ring carbon C2, more costly); (ii) tau2 = C10-C11-C13-O15 anti (O15...C10 ~3.75-3.85 A) is better than gauche (~2.95-3.15 A).
Groups: extended tau2 with C13 anti to C2: 6, 7, 21, 1, 17, 3 (only one cheap gauche). Extended tau2 but C13 anti to O9 (gauche to C2): 27, 30. Two gauche with cheap tau1: 13, 22, 15, 26, 9, 4, 18, 24. Two gauche with the more expensive tau1 (chain gauche to the methyl-bearing C2): 19, 5, 20, 2, 12, 16, 25, 10 - these also show the shortest methyl-to-chain contacts (C1...C13 3.4-3.5 A in 10 and 25).

Third, minor factor: the cis-substituent eclipsing measured by C1...C11. Values cluster at 2.98-3.07 A; conformers 24 (2.89 A, C1-C2-C10-C11 torsion ~0, fully eclipsed methyl/chain) and 28 (2.88 A) are the most strained in this respect, while 19, 5, 8, 10, 30 (3.07-3.12) are the most relaxed. Ring pucker (judged from the C11...C6 1,4 distance, 3.1 A = chain more pseudo-axial, 3.6 A = more pseudo-equatorial) gives only ~0.3 kcal-level differences and was used only to break ties inside the non-H-bonded groups (pseudo-equatorial chain favoured, e.g. 6, 7, 27 over 1, 17, 3, 30).

Ranking logic: the six H-bonded conformers first (ordered by H-bond length/linearity, with small penalties for the tight tau1 contacts in 8, O9...C13 2.78 A, and 23, 2.70 A, and for the eclipsed cis pair in 28); then the singly-gauche, extended-chain conformers; conf 13 inserted among them because its weak bent OH...O contact roughly offsets its second gauche; then the extended conformers with the chain gauche to C2 (27, 30); then the doubly-gauche folded conformers, with the ones that additionally suffer methyl/chain compression (24, 10, 25) lowest.

Uncertainty: the 6 H-bonded conformers are clearly separated from the rest (~2 kcal/mol), but within that set the differences are only ~0.2-0.5 kcal/mol, and the entire non-H-bonded block spans perhaps 1-1.5 kcal/mol, so the ordering there (especially inside groups of equal gauche count) is soft and could easily permute.

Connectivity (identical in all files) is CH3-CH(CHO)-CH2-O-CH=NH: an isobutyraldehyde-type CH bearing a methyl, an aldehyde (C6=O7, H8) and a CH2-O-CH=NH formimidate ester. The soft degrees of freedom are (i) tB = C6-C5-C9-O12 (backbone C-C), (ii) tC = C5-C9-O12-C13 (the C-C-O-C ester/ether torsion, which strongly prefers anti, ~1 kcal over gauche), (iii) which substituent on C5 (CHO, CH3 or H17) is anti to the ether O, and (iv) rotation of the CHO. I computed these torsions plus key nonbonded distances for all 30 structures. Results: tC is anti (170-180 deg) in 25(174), 20(180), 16(180), 8(171), 17(177), 9(178), 23(177), 22(177); gauche (72-81) in 19,11,2,26,6,29,13; and in the strained 90-110 region (rising toward the C-C-O-C barrier) in 5,18,28,30,1,12,21,14,27,7,10. Only conformer 25 has BOTH tB (165) and tC (174) anti, giving a fully extended, contact-free chain -> most stable. Checking the C5 substituent anti to O12 (O12...C1 distance: ~3.75 A = anti, ~2.95 A = gauche): 16,20,8,26,6,29,28,18,5,7,10 have the methyl anti (good); 25,11,2,19,12,27 have the CHO anti (good); while 17,9,23,22,30,1,21,14,3,15 place H17 anti, i.e. BOTH carbon substituents gauche to the ether oxygen (extra ~0.5-1 kcal of gauche strain). Gauche tB additionally brings the ether O within 2.85-2.95 A of the carbonyl carbon (mild dipolar/steric contact, e.g. 16, 20, 8, 17, 9). A distinct, clearly high-energy family exists: conformers 4, 24, 3 and 15 are folded so that the imidate nitrogen lone pair points at the aldehyde carbon with N...C6 = 2.10-2.13 A and N...O7 = 2.64-2.68 A, far inside van der Waals contact; the aldehyde carbon is pyramidalized by ~16 deg in these structures (partial nucleophilic addition, six-membered zwitterion-like closure), and their tC values are also badly compressed (48-59 deg). These four must be the least stable, with 4 (N...C 2.10, tC 48) and 3 worst. An intermediate group (5: N...C6 2.84; 18: 2.92; 28: 3.03) shows the same fold but only weakly, at the cost of a distorted tC ~90-96 deg, so they sit just above the strongly folded set. No conformer offers a genuine N-H...O=C hydrogen bond (the N-H is anti to the ester O in all structures and the shortest H15...O7 distances, ~2.8-3.2 A in the folded forms, are not aligned), so no conformer gains H-bond stabilization; conformer 13 is also penalized by an eclipsing-region tB of 127 deg. Uncertainty: the differences among the top ~12 extended conformers are small (a few tenths of a kcal), and the relative weight of 'tC anti + both-C-gauche' versus 'tB anti + tC gauche' is the main ambiguity; also, if the short N...C=O contacts in 3/4/15/24 were genuinely stabilizing n->pi* interactions rather than clashes, those four would move up sharply.

STRUCTURE: All files contain the same skeleton (atoms 1 = CH3, 5-10 = ring, C6=C7 the alkene (bond 1.32 A), 13 = exocyclic CH2, 14 = O, 15 = OH hydrogen). So the molecule is a cyclohexene bearing a methyl on the allylic ring carbon (atom 5) and a CH2OH on the homoallylic carbon (atom 9); these two ring carbons are 1,3 to each other (separated by C10). C8H14O, one ring + one C=C.

DIAGNOSTICS USED: (i) Ring pucker: the fragment C5-C6=C7-C8 is essentially planar in every structure (torsion ~0-2 deg), so I computed the signed out-of-plane displacements of C9 and C10 from that plane, Delta = d9 - d10. A proper half-chair gives |Delta| ~ 0.65-0.78 A (verified by torsion C8-C9-C10-C5 = 57-64 deg); a boat gives Delta ~ 0 (torsion 0-10 deg); twist forms give Delta ~ 0.1-0.35 (torsion 20-26 deg). (ii) Substituent orientation: d(C1...C13) ~ 5.0 A = both substituents pseudo-equatorial; ~3.4 A = the cis-1,3-diaxial arrangement (a genuine Me/CH2OH 1,3-diaxial clash, worth roughly 4-5 kcal/mol). (iii) Rotamer of the CH2OH arm from d(O...C8)/d(O...C10): both ~3.0 A means O anti to the ring C-H (preferred, as in ethylcyclohexane); one ~3.75 A means O anti to a ring carbon (slightly worse). (iv) Intramolecular O-H...pi contacts to the C6=C7 bond (H15 to alkene carbons).

RESULTS: Half-chair + di-equatorial (best family): 28, 25, 11, 2, 12, 3, 8, 21, 24 (Delta = 0.77-0.78, C1...C13 = 4.98-5.06). Of these, 28, 25 and 11 also have the favoured arm rotamer (O anti to H-C9, both O...Cring ~2.95-3.03 A); 2, 12, 3 have O anti to C10 and 8, 21, 24 have O anti to C8 (one extra gauche interaction, ~0.5 kcal). No short nonbonded contacts in any of them.
Half-chair + di-AXIAL: 4, 13, 18, 14, 20, 9, 1, 10 (Delta = +0.65 to +0.68, C1...C13 = 3.38-3.51). All carry the syn-1,3-diaxial Me/CH2OH clash. Two of them recover part of that cost with a clear O-H...pi hydrogen bond: 20 (H15...C6 2.40, H15...C7 2.39, H to alkene midpoint 2.30 A) and 10 (H15...C7 2.33, H15...C6 2.67 A); the rest (4, 13, 18, 14, 9, 1) have the OH pointing into free space and are the most strained set.
Boat / twist rings: 30, 29, 16, 23, 19, 22, 6, 17, 7 have Delta ~ 0 (C8-C9-C10-C5 eclipsed, 2-10 deg) = true boats; 26 (Delta 0.34, tors 26 deg), 5 (0.18, 21 deg), 27 (-0.19, 26 deg), 15 (-0.11) are twist forms, i.e. less torsional strain than a full boat. Compensating interactions: 16 has a good O-H...pi bond (H15...C7 2.33 A), 26 a weaker one (H15...C6 2.49 A), 23 and 7 only marginal O...C7 ~2.96/H15...C7 ~2.61 A contacts with poor O-H alignment. Two structures are additionally penalised because the methyl sits in the flagpole position over the ring (d(C1...C8) 3.35 A instead of the normal 4.25-4.30 A): 17 (boat, methyl flagpole, C1...C13 3.93) and 5 (twist, methyl flagpole plus a 3.57 A Me/CH2OH contact) - these are the worst geometries.

ENERGY ORDERING LOGIC: di-equatorial half-chairs (0-0.8 kcal, ordered by arm rotamer) < twist rings, especially those with an OH...pi bond (2-3) < diaxial half-chairs that are OH...pi stabilised (~3) < boats with partial/no H-bond (3.5-4.2) < unstabilised diaxial half-chairs (~5) < flagpole-methyl twist/boat (>5).

UNCERTAINTY: the nine di-equatorial half-chairs differ by only a few tenths of a kcal (rotamer of the CH2OH arm and of the O-H), so their internal order is soft. The relative placement of "boat ring" versus "di-axial half-chair" is the largest uncertainty (both ~3-5 kcal); I ranked the O-H...pi-stabilised twist/boat and diaxial structures above the plain boats, and the plain diaxial ones last except for the two flagpole-methyl cases.

Structure: all 30 files are the same molecule, HO-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH2-NH-CHO (N-(4-hydroxy-3-methylbutyl)formamide). Checking the C7-N-C9=O torsion (C7...O10 = 2.77-2.87 A in every conformer, C7...H(formyl) ~3.4 A) shows ALL structures have the favorable trans(Z) secondary amide, so no cis-amide penalty differentiates them. Therefore the ranking is governed by (a) intramolecular hydrogen bonding and (b) backbone torsional strain (gauche count, near-eclipsed torsions).

H-bond survey (donor H...acceptor distance and X-H...Y angle, computed from coordinates):
OH(hydroxyl) -> O=C(amide), the strongest possible interaction here (good donor + strong amide carbonyl acceptor, 9-membered chelate ring): 20 (1.87 A, 162 deg), 7 (1.90, 158), 24 (1.92, 166), 3 (1.92, 169), 29 (1.92, 169), 28 (1.94, 155), 4 (1.98, 174), 17 (2.00, 173), 8 (2.09, 147), 11 (2.10, 146).
N-H(amide) -> O(hydroxyl), a weaker donor/acceptor pair (7-membered ring): 5 (1.91, 147), 9 (1.92, 144), 14 (1.93, 143), 27 (2.02, 145), 16 (2.03, 146), 19 (2.17, 128), 25 (2.18, 130).
No H-bond at all (all donor-acceptor H...O > 2.4 A): 1, 2, 6, 10, 12, 13, 15, 18, 21, 22, 23, 26, 30 (23 and 18 have only long, badly angled NH...O contacts of 2.66 and 2.45 A, worth little).

- 24: excellent H-bond but O19-C18-C5-C6 is eclipsed (calculated 120 deg, O eclipsing H/CH3) -> ~1 kcal penalty.
- 7 (d1 = 3.55, eclipsed) and 20 (d1 = 106 deg, d3 ~100, d4 3.51) have the shortest H...O contacts but pay torsional strain for wrapping the chain.
- 8, 11: OH...O=C strongly bent (~146 deg, 2.09-2.10 A), so only a partial H-bond; 11 additionally has an anti O-C-C-C that keeps the OH from reaching properly.
- 5, 9, 14: well-formed NH...OH (1.91-1.93 A) with normal gauche/gauche/gauche skeletons.
- 27, 16: same motif but 0.1 A longer and one near-eclipsed C6-C7 / C7-N torsion (d4 = 3.58-3.59).

- Among the non-H-bonded set the discriminator is chain extension: 15, 1, 10, 2, 21, 13, 26, 22, 30 all show only two gauche torsions with one anti (most extended, no 1,5 clashes; O...O separations >5 A so no dipole repulsion), whereas 12 and 23 add a third gauche/eclipsed torsion, and 6 (three gauche + d4 = 3.54) and 18 (three gauche + d4 = 3.62, eclipsed) are the most torsionally strained and H-bond-free, hence least stable.

Uncertainties: the energy gap between a bent OH...O=C (8, 11) and a good NH...OH (5, 9, 14) is small and could reverse; ordering inside the strongly H-bonded block (4, 17, 29, 3, 28, 24, 7, 20) rests on ~0.5 kcal differences in H-bond linearity vs. one eclipsed torsion; and the nine non-H-bonded 'two-gauche' conformers (15, 1, 10, 2, 21, 13, 26, 22, 30) are essentially isoenergetic, so their internal order is the least reliable part of the list.

Connectivity (identical in all files): CH3–C5H(–C6H2–O7H)–C12H(–O20H)–C13H(aziridine ring C13–C14H2–N15H). The molecule therefore has two OH donors, one NH donor, and O/N acceptors. Because O7 and O20 sit in a 1,3-type relationship (O7–C6–C5–C12–O20), the dominant stabilizing motif available is a five-membered O–H...O hydrogen bond; a second, larger motif (O7–H...N15, 7-membered) and a weak five-membered N15–H...O20 contact are also possible.

I measured, for every conformer, H8...O20, H21...O7, H8/H21...N15 and H16...O7/O20 distances plus the X–H...Y angles.

(a) Genuine O–H...O hydrogen bonds (O...O 2.76–2.82 A, H...O 1.93–2.08 A, angle 128–143 deg) are present in 3, 12, 29, 16, 21, 14, 17, 9, 13, 24, 4, 2, 28, 6, 22, 5, 19, 25, 11. Their quality varies: 3 is best (H...O 1.93, 143 deg), followed by 12 (1.95/141), 16 (1.96/141), 21 (1.96/140), 29 (1.96/140), 14 (1.96/140), 17 (1.98/140), 9 (1.98/138), 13 (2.01/138), 24 (2.01/137); the bent, longer ones are 25 (2.06/130) and 11 (2.08/128).

(b) Conformer 23 lacks the diol bond but has a well-directed O7–H...N15 bond (H...N 2.13, N...O 3.01, 151 deg) closing a 7-membered ring. Aziridine N is a weaker base than a normal amine, so I score this comparable to, but not better than, the best O–H...O cases.

(c) Several conformers add a weak five-membered N15–H...O20 contact (H...O 2.26–2.36 A but forced angles of only ~105 deg): 3, 2, 28, 4, 29, 19, 22, 23. Conformer 12 has a somewhat better secondary N–H...O7 approach (2.65 A, ~117 deg) to the same oxygen that already accepts the strong OH bond, i.e. a mildly cooperative arrangement, so 12 ranks just below 3.

(d) Ten conformers have no hydrogen bond at all: their two hydroxyls point into space with O...O separations of 3.0–4.9 A (15, 26, 8, 7, 27, 1, 18, 10, 20, 30). Losing the ~3–4 kcal/mol intramolecular OH...O bond puts all of them below the H-bonded set. Within this group 30 retains a long/bent OH...O contact (H...O 2.40, 122 deg, O...O 3.03) and 7 a very weak one (2.89 A, 114 deg) plus a folded, vdW-compact backbone, so these two are least penalized; 20 (O...O 3.80) still has some electrostatic pairing, whereas 15, 27, 18, 26, 10, 8 and especially the fully extended 1 (O...O 4.89) have completely uncompensated, divergent OH dipoles.

(e) Torsional check: substituent-substituent distances across C5–C12 (C...C ~3.0–3.1 A for gauche, ~3.85 A for anti) show all conformers are essentially staggered; no eclipsed backbone or short H...H (<2.0 A) clash was found, so ring strain of the aziridine is constant and sterics only fine-tune the order. The remaining discriminators (0.05 A in H...O, ~10 deg in angle, presence of the weak NH contact) are small, so differences within the H-bonded block, and the internal order of the non-bonded block, are uncertain (probably <1 kcal/mol in many pairs). The clear, robust statement is: H-bonded (diol or OH...N) conformers first, dangling-OH conformers last.

All 30 structures are the same molecule: an O-alkyl acetimidate, CH3-C(=NH)-O-CH2CH2CH2CH2-OH (atoms 1-11 in every file are CH3, C(=N), N, N-H, ester-type O, C6, C7, C8, C9, O(H), H(O)). Ring strain is absent, and in every conformer the imidate unit is essentially planar with the N=C-O-C torsion near 0 deg (Z-type, the normal ester/imidate arrangement), so the discriminating factors are (i) intramolecular O-H...X hydrogen bonding, and (ii) the number of gauche/skew torsions along the O-CH2CH2CH2CH2-OH chain (T1 = C2-O5-C6-C7, T2 = O5-C6-C7-C8, T3 = C6-C7-C8-C9, T4 = C7-C8-C9-O10). I estimated torsion types from the 1,4 heavy-atom distances (anti ~3.7-3.9 A, gauche/skew ~2.9-3.3 A) and checked H...acceptor distances plus O-H...O angles.

Hydrogen bonds found (hydroxyl H to the imidate ether O, an S(7)-type ring):
- 5: H...O 1.87 A, O-H...O 158 deg, and T1 anti -> best combination of a nearly linear H-bond with the preferred anti C-O-C-C torsion.
- 9: H...O 1.90 A, 154 deg, T1 near-anti (C2...C7 3.55).
- 13: H...O 1.90 A, 153 deg, but T1 gauche (~80 deg).
- 8: H...O 2.02 A, 154 deg, T1 gauche.
- 17: H...O 2.08 A but a bent 138 deg angle (weaker), compensated by T1 anti.
- 2: H...O 2.22 A, 138 deg (O...O 3.01) - a genuine but mediocre H-bond, and the chain is all-gauche, so most of the gain is eaten by torsional strain.
- 7: O-H points at the imine N but at 3.23 A (too long) and only a 118 deg, 2.78 A contact to the ester O -> essentially only weak electrostatics.
- 18: no O-H...X bond, but the imine N-H reaches the hydroxyl O (H...O 2.44 A, N-H...O 128 deg), a weak bent H-bond; its chain is all gauche.
- 6 (3.26 A) and 25 (3.16 A) show only long, badly oriented O(H)...O contacts (no real bond).

Torsional bookkeeping for the non-H-bonded set (gauche among T2-T4, plus T1):
- 30: T2, T3, T4 all anti (3.78-3.89) with only T1 gauche -> the fully extended, sterically cleanest conformer; no H-bond but almost no torsional strain.
- Two-anti chains with T1 gauche: 3, 1, 12, 26.
- T1 anti with two chain gauche: 20, 23, 11.
- One chain anti + T1 gauche (two gauche + T1): 10, 19, 21, 15, 24, 29, 28, 22, 14.
- T1 anti but three chain gauche: 6.
- Fully coiled, three chain gauche + T1 gauche and no compensating H-bond: 27, 4, 16, 25 (25 and 7 at least have a long O(H)...O contact; 27, 4, 16 have the hydroxyl pointing into free space, so their folding buys nothing).

No structure shows an unusually short nonbonded H...H contact (<2.0 A) or O...O repulsion without a bridging H, so clashes are not decisive; 2 and 7 have 3.0-3.3 A O...O approaches that are only marginally stabilized by the poorly aligned OH.

Balancing a good intramolecular O-H...O bond (worth roughly 2-3.5 kcal/mol here) against ~0.8 kcal/mol per gauche torsion gives: strongly H-bonded folded conformers first (5, 9, 13, 8, 17), then the strain-free extended 30, then the weakly H-bonded 2, then the low-gauche extended family (20, 23, 11, 3, 1, 12, 26), then weakly N-H bonded 18 and the more coiled non-bonded structures, with the fully coiled, non-H-bonded 27, 16, 4, 25 last. Uncertainty: the 13/8/17 and the 20/23/11/3/1/12/26 blocks are nearly isoenergetic (differences well under 1 kcal/mol), and the trade-off between the H-bond in 2 and the strain-free extended 30 is within the error of this analysis; the ordering inside the large 'one-anti' block (10, 19, 21, 15, 24, 29, 28, 22, 14) is essentially arbitrary.

All 30 structures are the same molecule, cyanomethyl 2-cyclopropylethyl ether, N≡C-CH2-O-CH2-CH2-(c-C3H5). Connectivity checks (C7-C8 1.50, C7-C9 1.49, C8-C9 1.50 Å) confirm an intact cyclopropane in every conformer, so ring strain is constant and the energy differences must come from four torsions plus 1,5 (syn-pentane-type) contacts:
T2 = C(N)-CH2-O-CH2, T3 = CH2-O-CH2-CH2, T4 = O-CH2-CH2-CH(ring), T5 = ring orientation.
I classified each torsion from the 1,4 distances (calibrated on structures whose torsions I computed exactly): for C-C-O-C anti ~3.62-3.68 Å, gauche ~2.90-2.95 Å; for O-C-C-C anti ~3.73-3.81 Å, gauche ~2.95-3.07 Å; intermediate distances (3.1-3.4 Å) correspond to distorted, partly eclipsed torsions (80-100 deg, verified by explicit dihedral calculations for 1, 8, 9, 21, 27, 29).
I also measured the two 1,5 distances (C2...C6 for the T2/T3 pair, C3...C7 for the T3/T4 pair). Calibration: anti/anti 4.7 Å, anti/gauche 4.3-4.4 Å, gauche/gauche same sign 3.7-3.9 Å, gauche/gauche opposite sign (syn-pentane clash) 3.1-3.4 Å.
Results: (T2,T3,T4) = 13 (g,a,a), 6 (g,a,a), 16 (a,a,a), 30 (a,a,a) are fully staggered with no compressed 1,5 contacts -> most stable. Since the OCH2CN unit gains a small anomeric/gauche stabilization (O lone pair antiperiplanar to the C-CN bond), I place the two gauche-T2/anti-anti forms (13, 6) marginally above the all-anti ones (16, 30); this 0.2-0.4 kcal ordering is the least certain part of the ranking.
Next come the (g,a,g) set 15, 22, 18, 7, 24 (single gauche about the O-CH2-CH2-C bond, C3...C7 = 4.20-4.24 Å, no clashes), then 17 (a,a,g).
Then conformers with one gauche C-O-C-C torsion, which costs ~1.2 kcal: 3 and 12 (g,g,a; 3 is clean at d(C2...C6)=3.74, 12 is slightly compressed at 3.62), then 5, 23, 28 (a,g,a; clean, but they lose the anomeric gauche at T2).
All-gauche but all-staggered, same-sign structures 11, 14, 20, 26 pay three gauche penalties (~1.8 kcal) yet have no short contacts (d = 3.7-3.9 Å); 25 (a,g,g) is similar but also anti at T2.
A distinct 'folded' family (1, 4, 10, 19, 2, 29) has the nitrile bent back over the chain: T2 is distorted to 80-85 deg and C2...C6 is squeezed to 3.08-3.20 Å (syn-pentane-like), only partly compensated by a weak intramolecular C-H...N contact of 2.75-2.90 Å. I therefore rank them just below the clean all-gauche set: 1, 4, 10 keep T4 anti (best of this family), 19 and 2 add a gauche T4, and 29 has both a strongly distorted T3 (82 deg) and the tightest 3.20 Å compression.
Worst are conformers with eclipsing-region torsions and compressed C3...C7 contacts in the alkyl part, where no H-bond-like compensation exists: 27 (T4 = 98 deg, C3...C7 3.39), 21 (T3 = 99 deg, C3...C7 3.35), 9 (T3 = 88, T4 = 80 deg, C3...C7 3.25), and 8, which is the only structure with BOTH 1,5 compressions (C2...C6 3.21 and C3...C7 3.40) together with two near-eclipsed torsions (T2 90, T4 94 deg) - clearly the least stable.
Uncertainties: (i) whether the anomeric gauche at O-CH2-CN really outweighs anti (affects the 13/6 vs 16/30 and 3/12 vs 5/23/28 orderings by a few tenths of a kcal); (ii) the balance between the syn-pentane compression and the weak C-H...N/dipole stabilization in the folded family (1, 4, 10, 19, 2, 29), which could move them up several places; (iii) cyclopropyl rotamer differences (T5) are <0.5 kcal and were used only as a tiebreaker, so near-degenerate pairs like 13/6, 16/30 and within the (g,a,g) and (g,g,g) sets are essentially interchangeable.

STRUCTURE. All 30 files have the same atom ordering: O1(H2) is a hydroxyl on C3 (an exocyclic CH2OH); C4 is a fully substituted sp2 carbon (C4=C5, C5 carries H19); the ring is C4=C5-C6H2-C8H2-C10H2-O11-C12H2-C4, i.e. a seven-membered oxepine ring (cis C=C inside the ring) bearing a hydroxymethyl group on the alkene carbon that is also attached to the O-CH2 (C12). So the only conformational degrees of freedom are (i) the 7-ring pucker, (ii) the allylic torsion O1-C3-C4=C5, and (iii) the O-H rotation.

METHOD. Since torsion signs cannot be read off by eye, I used 1,4-distances as calibrated proxies for the ring torsions (for C-C-C-C: 2.68 A = eclipsed 0 deg, 3.03 = 60 deg, 3.34 = 90 deg, 3.90 = anti; slightly shorter values for C-C-C-O / C-C-O-C). I evaluated A=d(C5,C10) (C6-C8 torsion), B=d(C6,O11) (C8-C10), C=d(C8,C12) (C10-O11), D=d(C10,C4) (O11-C12), plus O1...O11, H2...O11 and H2...midpoint(C4=C5).

RING FAMILIES. The 30 structures collapse into exactly four ring conformers (each appearing as both enantiomeric puckers with several CH2OH rotamers):
(I) A~3.19, B~3.11, C~3.07, D~3.14 -> all four sp3 torsions 70-85 deg, no eclipsing at all (a relaxed twist-chair): conformers 23, 17, 20, 30, 26, 18, 10, 22, 19.
(IV) A~2.90, B~3.29, C~2.81, D~2.87 -> C10-O11 torsion only ~42 deg (partly eclipsed, but a low-barrier C-O bond) and C8-C10-O11 near 95 deg: 21, 2, 12, 24, 8.
(II) A~3.22, B~2.80, C~2.90, D~3.18 -> C8-C10 (CH2-CH2) torsion ~40 deg, i.e. genuine C-C eclipsing strain: 15, 11, 28, 13, 7, 25, 29, 3.
(III) A~2.95, B~2.70, C~3.24, D~2.88 -> C8-C10 torsion only ~30 deg (worst C-C eclipse) plus a ~95 deg C-C-O-C torsion: 5, 27, 4, 6, 16, 9, 1, 14.
Summing simple threefold torsional terms gives I (~2.3) < II ~ IV (~2.5) < III (~3.3 kcal/mol-ish), so family III is clearly the strained set and family I the most relaxed; II and IV are nearly degenerate and their placement is the least certain part of this ranking.

OH ORIENTATION. No conformer achieves a real O-H...O(ether) hydrogen bond: the shortest H2...O11 contacts are 2.92 A/129 deg (conf 20) and 2.89 A/127 deg (conf 12) - only marginally attractive; all others have H2...O11 > 3.3 A (O1...O11 3.5-4.9 A), so the potential six-membered O-H...O ring is never closed. The discriminating feature is instead the allylic rotamer: d(O1,C5) ~2.73-2.82 means O1 is syn-periplanar to the alkene C-H (least hindered, allyl-alcohol-like), whereas d(O1,C5) 3.35-3.56 means O1 eclipses the bulkier ring CH2-O (C12) group. In eight structures (23, 17, 21, 2, 15, 11, 9, 1) the hydroxyl H additionally sits 2.6 A from the C4=C5 midpoint (H...C4 2.6, H...C5 2.8, ~1.0 A out of the alkene plane) - a weak O-H...pi contact combined with the favourable syn rotamer. These get a small bonus. Conformers 30 and 28 have the good syn rotamer but the O-H rotated outward (H...pi 3.4), i.e. no bonus. No abnormally short H...H or transannular contacts were found in any structure (closest O...H(C12) contacts 2.4-2.6 A are normal).

RANKING LOGIC. Primary key = ring family (I < IV ~ II < III); secondary key = OH environment (O-H...pi/syn rotamer > weak O-H...O > syn with OH out > anti rotamer where O1 eclipses the ring OCH2 and sits 3.5-3.7 A from the ether O with unfavourable O/O dipole contact). Because the ring-family energy spread (a few tenths of a kcal between I, II, IV) is comparable to the OH-orientation effect, the two pi-bonded members of families IV and II (21, 2, 15, 11) are placed just after the whole family-I block rather than deep in their own families; this interleaving, and the II vs IV order, are the main uncertainties. Family III (30 deg C-C eclipse) is confidently last, with its two pi-stabilized members (9, 1) leading that block.

All 30 files share the same skeleton: a fused bicyclic cage in which an oxetane ring (C4-C5-O12-C6, atoms 7-9-12-13) and a cyclobutane ring (C3-C4-C6-C7, atoms 5-7-13-15) share the C4-C6 edge (a 2-oxabicyclo[2.2.0]hexane), carrying a 2-hydroxyethyl chain (C2H4OH, atoms 4-3-1-2) on the cyclobutane carbon C3 (atom 5). Checking the sign of the substituent relative to the cyclobutane plane in several structures (30, 9, 4) shows the chain is always on the same (concave/endo) face as the oxetane bridge, i.e. the stereochemistry is preserved; the cage geometry (bond lengths, puckers) is essentially identical in all files. Therefore the entire energy spread comes from (i) the intramolecular O-H...O(ether) hydrogen bond, (ii) the C3-C2-C1-O torsion (anti vs gauche vs distorted), (iii) the C(ring)-C3-C2-C1 rotamer (whether the chain is folded over the cage, and whether it eclipses a ring bond), and (iv) 1,5-type contacts of the chain with the endo oxetane CH2 hydrogen H10 and with C7-H17.

H-bond survey: computed H2...O12 distances are >4 A for every structure except two. Conformer 9: H2...O12 = 2.00 A, O1...O12 = 2.94 A, O-H...O angle ~162 deg - a genuinely good hydrogen bond closing an 8-membered pseudo-ring (chain folded over the oxetane), with its shortest other contact only H2...H10 = 2.32 A. Conformer 16: H2...O12 = 2.06 A, O...O = 2.95 A, but the angle is poorer (~151 deg) and it pays two 2.16 A H...H contacts (H2/H10 and H20/H17) plus a distorted O-C1-C2-C3 torsion (~85 deg). So 9 > 16, and both are clearly the most stable (a 3-4 kcal/mol type bonus).

Chain torsion C3-C2-C1-O (proxied by the O1...C3 1-4 distance, ~3.7-3.85 A = anti, ~2.9-3.1 A = gauche): anti in 23, 12, 24, 25, 10, 22, 11, 19, 14; normal gauche (60-70 deg) in 30, 27, 29, 21, 13, 15, 28, 2, 3, 4, 6, 18, 17, 1, 20, 9; and strained intermediate values in 7 (77 deg), 5 (85 deg), 8 (83 deg), 26 (111 deg), which sit near the eclipsing/anticlinal region and are penalized.

Contacts: essentially every conformer has one mildly repulsive H...H of 2.1-2.3 A between a chain hydrogen (H18/H19/H20/H21 or the hydroxyl) and the endo oxetane hydrogen H10 or the C7 hydrogen H17 - unavoidable crowding for an endo substituent. More serious are C...H approaches of ~2.53-2.60 A (C1 against H17 or H10) in 24, 14, 1, 20, 8, 26, indicating the chain is folded down onto the cage. Conformer 10 additionally has C1 almost eclipsing the C3-C7 ring bond (torsion ~13 deg), which offsets its favourable anti O-C-C-C. Conformers 30, 27, 29, 21 are the cleanest non-H-bonded gauche forms (no contact below ~2.4 A, chain anti to a ring carbon, extended away from the cage). Several structures (5, 26, 1, 20) place the hydroxyl oxygen 2.15-2.35 A from H10, a weak CH...O contact that is at best marginally stabilizing and here is combined with torsional distortion.

Ranking logic: H-bonded (9, 16) first; then non-H-bonded conformers with anti O-C-C-C and only ~2.2 A H...H contacts (19, 22, 11, 12, 25, 23); then anti-chain forms that pay a C...H ~2.6 A fold-down penalty (14, 24); then the clean gauche forms (27, 29, 30, 21); then gauche forms with 2.15-2.3 A contacts (4, 3, 2, 1, 28, 13, 15, 6, 18, 17); finally the torsionally distorted/eclipsed and sterically pinched ones (10, 7, 5, 20, 26, 8).

Uncertainty: apart from the two hydrogen-bonded structures, the spread is probably under ~1 kcal/mol, and the ordering within the anti group, within the clean-gauche group, and within the 2.15-2.3 A contact group is essentially within the noise of this geometric analysis; dipole-dipole alignment between the C-O-H and the ether C-O-C could easily reshuffle those middle entries.

All 30 files describe cis-3-(2-hydroxyethyl)cyclobutan-1-ol: a cyclobutane ring (atoms 5,7,10,13) bearing an OH on C10 (O11-H12) and a -CH2CH2OH chain (C4-C3-O1-H2) on C5, the two substituents lying on the same face of the (nearly planar) ring in every structure. Ring strain is therefore constant, so the ranking is dominated by (i) the presence/quality of the intramolecular O-H...O hydrogen bond that the cis-1,3 arrangement permits, and (ii) torsional quality of the two-carbon chain (O1-C3-C4-C5 dihedral, judged from the O1...C5(ring-carbon) 1,4 distance: ~3.0 A = gauche, ~3.8 A = anti, 3.2-3.35 A = half-eclipsed/skew).

H-bond survey (O1...O11 and H...O): only four conformers have O...O < 3.3 A: 30 (O...O 2.88, H2...O11 1.92, O-H...O 171 deg), 1 (2.87, 1.91, 169 deg), 9 (2.89, H12...O1 1.94, 163 deg), 25 (2.92, H12...O1 1.99, 160 deg). All other conformers have the two oxygens 3.8-6.6 A apart with the O-H vectors pointing away, i.e. no H-bond at all. The four H-bonded structures are therefore clearly the most stable (roughly 3-4 kcal/mol advantage). Within this set, 1 and 30 use the primary (chain) OH as donor to the more basic secondary ring alcohol oxygen and have the most linear, shortest contacts (1.91/169, 1.92/171); 9 and 25 have the reverse (secondary donor to primary acceptor) with longer and more bent bridges (1.94/163 and 1.99/160). The chain torsion in 1 (58 deg) is slightly better staggered than in 30 (64 deg), so 1 is put marginally first; this pair is essentially degenerate.

Non-bonded set: the chain is fully staggered/anti (O1...Cring 3.74-3.81 A, i.e. dihedral ~165-175 deg) in 13, 10, 15, 18, 23, 16, 26. These extended conformers have no eclipsing, no short nonbonded contacts (all intramolecular H...H > 2.1 A) and the two hydroxyl dipoles maximally separated (O...O 5.7-6.6 A), so they are the best of the non-H-bonded group. Slight preference is given to those with the largest O-O separation and cleanest anti chain (15, 18, 16, 26, 23) over 10 and 13 (13 has the two OH groups closest, 5.7 A, with no compensating H-bond).

A large family has a gauche chain (O1...Cring 2.95-3.11 A, dihedral 55-70 deg) but the oxygens far apart (5.2-6.3 A), so the gauche penalty (~0.4-0.6 kcal/mol) is uncompensated: 4, 29, 6, 3, 8, 22, 20, 21, 5, 19, 7, 2, 24, 27, 14.
